conventions: Rule 31's subtraction test was run on this chapter's recurring nominal renderings and is settled: `פֶּסֶל` → *graven image* heads on *graven* (JDG.18.14, 17, 18, 20, 30, 31), `מַסֵּכָה` → *molten image* on *molten* (14, 17, 18), `נַעַר` → *young man* on *young* (3, 15), and `טַף` → *little ones* on *little* (21). The ASV nowhere writes *image*, *man* or *ones* alone for these words, so the generic noun is the supplied completion in each. The competing head is that generic noun in every case; do not re-open it verse by verse.

A supplied English subject *it* with its copula joins the predicate's unit where the clause has a subject the *it* denotes — `טוֹבָה` → *it is very good* (JDG.18.9) and `אַחֲרֵי` → *it is behind*, on the preposition under rule 49 (JDG.18.12) — while the anticipatory *it* of *is it better ... to be priest* (JDG.18.19) is its own `added` unit under rule 25, because the ASV renders the extraposed infinitival subject in full. Read whether the clause's real subject stands elsewhere in the English before placing such an *it*.

In `מַה־לְּ` with a suffix, the verb the ASV writes belongs to the preposition and the pronoun to the suffix, whichever verb it is: *hast thou* (JDG.18.3) and *have I* (JDG.18.24) under rule 43's possessive clause, *aileth thee* (JDG.18.23, 24) under rule 49's relational-verb sentence. The interrogative keeps only its own *What*, and the preposition is never left `unrepresented` here.

A possessive the ASV supplies on a bare noun is marked `added` in this chapter even where a co-referent pronominal suffix stands in the same clause and has already been rendered: the italic *their* of *their inheritance ... had not fallen unto them* (JDG.18.1) and the *his* of *asked him of his welfare* (JDG.18.15). The competing reading is rule 18's twice-realized suffix, which would fold each word into that suffix's discontinuous unit headed on *them* and *him* respectively; both verses take the `added` reading, and the ASV's italic corroborates it at JDG.18.1 only.

`מִשָּׁם` is divided by counting the ASV's words: *from thence* (JDG.18.11) spends a word on each morpheme, so rule 2 splits it and `מִן` takes *from*; the bare *thence* (JDG.18.13) meets rule 30's one-rendering condition, and the preposition and adverb share one unit headed on `שָׁם`, which carries the lexeme. The difference between the two verses is the ASV's and not an oversight.
report: Read all 69 candidate lemma groups and then the dump end to end for `added`-unit splits the lemma table cannot see. Every difference I found is licensed by the source or by what the ASV actually wrote; nothing is one construction analysed two ways.

Near-misses examined and cleared: `מִשָּׁם` split at v11 (*from thence*, a word per morpheme) and fused at v13 (bare *thence*) — rule 30's one-rendering condition, and both verses say so; `עִם־בֵּית מִיכָה` as *were by* at v3 (rule 49 copula in a main verbless clause) against *near to* at v22 (the copula already spent on the first relative, compound preposition headed on *near* by rule 24); `בֵּית מִיכָה` as *the house of Micah* (v2, 3, 13, 15, 22) against the possessive recasting *Micah's house* (v18, 22, 31), which rule 29 counts by the determiner standing before each word.

Waw plus discourse adverb: v14 writes two words and divides *now* to `עַתָּה`, *therefore* to the waw; v29 writes one, and *howbeit* writes `אוּלָם`'s own lexeme, so the adverb takes it and the waw is `unrepresented`. That is rule 14's own count, not two policies — though *howbeit* is a corpus waw-rendering elsewhere, so the note in v29 earns its place.

Phrasal particles: the two `added` *away*s at v24 sit against *went back* (v26), *enter in* (v9), *came in* (v17) and *spy out* (v2, 14, 17), all kept with their verbs. Rule 44 asks whether the bare English verb already writes the source lexeme; *taken* writes `לָקַח` and *gone* writes `הלך`, while *went* alone does not write `שׁוּב`'s returning. Licensed by lexeme, not inconsistent.

Supplied subordinators and coordinators are counted consistently: `added` where no conjunction stands (*When* at v3 and v22, *and* at v9 and twice at v17, under rules 55 and 14), and one rendering of a written waw where one does (*And when* v18, *and when* v26). Possessive clauses likewise: `הָיָה` takes the *had* at v27 with the `לְ` silent, and the bare `לְ` takes it at v3, v7, v24 and v28 with the suffix taking the subject pronoun — rule 43 throughout.

The two large-source-unit flags are genuinely indivisible: `אֲשֶׁר ... בָּהּ` → *wherein* (v6, headed on the relative) and `בְּקִרְבָּהּ` → *therein* (v7, headed on the construct `קֶרֶב`, which carries the lexeme, as rules 23 and 30 direct). `בָהּ` → *therein* at v28 heads on the preposition, which is rule 22's own division where no relative and no lexical noun stands.

BSB: 34 comparable disagreements, all documented convention differences — articles left unrepresented beside a demonstrative or as agreement articles (rules 41, 47), prepositions silenced by an ASV recasting (rule 40), unrendered waws, object markers, the paragogic he of v9, and the resumptive `שָׁם` of v10 and suffixes of v5 and v7. None is a genuine error.

The one BSB item with substance is v2 `בְּנֵי` in `אֲנָשִׁים בְּנֵי־חַיִל` → *men of valor*, marked `unrepresented` with the *of* going to the rectum under rule 19. The competing reading fuses `בְּנֵי חַיִל` on *of valor* under rule 30's `אִשָּׁה זוֹנָה` sentence, headed on `חַיִל`. Both are defensible, the verse defends its choice in a note, and I have not changed an accepted edge to move an aggregate.

One judgment a later reader should know I weighed and left: the supplied possessives of v1 (*their inheritance ... unto them*) and v15 (*asked him of his welfare*) are both `added`, though rule 18's twice-realized-suffix sentence (`מִכֶּם מָזוֹר` → *cure you of your wound*) would fold each into the co-referent suffix. The two verses agree with each other, so this is not a split; it is recorded as a convention with the competing reading named, and v15 is the weaker of the two, since the ASV italicizes only v1's *their*.

Verdict no-change refers to the alignments: no patches. Five conventions are appended, and the chapter taught nothing that generalises — every recurring judgment here is an application of rules 14, 30, 31, 40, 43 and 49 as they already stand, so promotions and amendments are empty.
